familysearch_id_note: This leaf is NOT in the project's FamilySearch deposit of 74 images and has no FamilySearch id. It is leaf n167 of NARA microfilm publication M704 roll 57, read off the Internet Archive's digitisation of that roll. T-0543 exhausted the deposit for printed 232's continuation and found none; T-0736/T-0911 found it on the film. The file is named for the leaf rather than for an id it does not have.
printed_page_note: A continuation (right) leaf carries no page stamp of its own. It is the right half of the opening whose left half is printed page 232, familysearch id 33S7-9YYJ-W6 — paired by T-0911 and not re-opened here.
division: the division allotted to S. W. Sherman, which is the town of Chicago
what_this_pass_read: Every one of the 31 ruled lines, in enumeration order, across the family TOTAL, the seven industry columns, the pensioners block, the ten deaf/dumb/blind/insane columns and the seven schools columns — the whole of the leaf but its final column, which is declared unread below. T-0911 read the two pairing keys and the first six figures of the TOTAL column and nothing else; this is the rest.
exposure_note: The film is better lit than the deposit's own scans and the ink is unambiguous, but the grain is heavy: the Allen County scan of this roll carries a dense speckle whose components are 2 to 4 px across, against 6 to 12 px for the enumerator's pen. Every crop read here was median-filtered at 3 px and background-subtracted against a 41-px Gaussian of itself before it was magnified; no reading was taken off the raw exposure and none was taken below 2.2x.
the_rules_of_this_leaf_lean: THE COLUMN GEOMETRY COULD NOT BE TAKEN IN ONE PROFILE, and this is the fault T-0761 is open on. tools/read_census_continuation.py exits with 'no industry run bracketed by TOTAL and PENSIONERS' on this leaf: a column-darkness profile over the whole body finds three vertical rules where the form has thirty-eight, because the printed rules do not stand square to the raster. Measured here, band by band: the TOTAL column's left rule stands at x1143 at y970 and at x1177 at y2790, so a rule leans 34 px over the body — more than half a column's width, which is why one profile over the whole height averages every rule away. The geometry below was therefore taken in 260-px bands, where a rule is straight enough to find, and the bands agree on a single linear model: x(y) = x(2270) + 0.021*(y-2270). Every crop this pass read was resampled through that model, so the columns stand square in the images the digits were read from and a guide drawn at a rule's x lands on the rule down the whole crop.

column_geometry.how: Vertical printed rules located band by band with the column-darkness profile of tools/read_census_continuation.py (cover 0.70, 260-px bands), then carried to a common y with the lean model above. Named against the printed headings, which were read directly rather than inferred: the header band was resampled square and rotated 90 degrees, and the seven industry labels read Mining. / Agriculture. / Commerce. / Manufactures and trades. / Navigation of the ocean. / Navigation of canals, lakes, and rivers. / Learned professions and engineers. — the printed order of the form, confirming the naming rather than assuming it.
column_geometry.slaves_block_note: The twelve slave columns stand left of x1170 and were read as a block; see blocks_carrying_no_entry.

row_grid.how: The row centres were taken from the ink of the TOTAL column, which is the one column with an entry on every line, and they came out UNIFORM — which is worth saying, because these leaves carry no horizontal rules between the heading and the footer and every previous reading has had to anchor its rows by cross-column coincidence. Thirty-one entries stand between y892 and y2952 with no gap and no doubled interval, and a straight line through the first and last predicts every one of the twenty-nine between them.
row_grid.residual: No entry's ink centre stands more than 12 px from its predicted centre, against a 68.67-px pitch. The grid is not in doubt anywhere on this leaf.
row_grid.count_note: 31 entries in the TOTAL column against printed 232's 31 ruled lines. This is one of T-0642's two pairing keys and T-0911 had already read it; it is restated here because this pass counted it again from the ink rather than taking it on.

footer_as_read.how: the enumerator's own footing row, y2975-3045, resampled square and read at 5x and 7x, cell by cell.
footer_as_read.blank_cells_note: mining, agriculture and navigation of the ocean are footed with an EMPTY cell and not with a nought, and are recorded as null rather than 0 — the sheet foots nothing there because nothing stands on the lines above.
footer_as_read.schools_and_ddbi_footings: The pensioners, deaf/dumb/blind/insane and schools blocks are footed with empty cells across every one of their nineteen columns. Read at 2.6x over the footer band: paper, printed rules and set-off, and no figure.

the_total_footing_settled.ticket_asked: T-0912's acceptance required the footing glyph T-0911 read as 195, with 198 as its arguable alternate, to be settled or to be recorded as unsettled with what it would take.
the_total_footing_settled.on_what_evidence: The third glyph carries a CLOSED UPPER LOOP joined to a lower bowl. This hand's 5 does not: its four 5s on this leaf (lines 1, 3, 14 and 30) are written with an open top stroke running right and a single bowl, with no closed loop anywhere. Its 8 does: line 23's TOTAL figure — which printed 232's own per-line count independently says is an 8 — has exactly the stacked double loop the footing's third glyph has. The comparison was made at 5x and 6x with the glyphs stacked side by side, and the discrimination is a matter of a closed loop being present or absent rather than of a judgement about a stroke's curvature.
the_total_footing_settled.what_would_overturn_it: A second, differently-lit exposure of this leaf. Only one digitisation of M704 roll 57 is public today, so there is no second look to be had at present; a NARA-supplied scan, or a different library's filming of the same roll, would settle it against a second hand of light.
the_total_footing_settled.what_it_does_not_change: The pairing. T-0911 recorded that the pairing of printed 232 to this leaf does NOT rest on the footing — it rests on the line-count key and the sequence screen — and this pass strengthens the second of those from six positions to all thirty-one while weakening the footing. The pairing is not re-opened here and is not re-ruled here. What the change DOES mean for T-0642's footing key is a question for the owner, and it is filed as its own ticket rather than decided in this one.

column_closure.what: the enumerator's printed footing against the sum of the lines this pass read, column by column.
column_closure.note: SEVEN OF THE EIGHT FOOTED COLUMNS CLOSE EXACTLY, on a reading made before any footing was consulted for a digit. Nothing here was adjusted to make a column close, and the one column that does not close is reported below rather than corrected.
column_closure.the_one_that_does_not_close: TOTAL. The enumerator foots 198; his own thirty-one lines sum to 193. That is the enumerator's arithmetic and not this pass's reading: the thirty-one figures are individually unambiguous, they are the same thirty-one numbers in the same order as printed 232's own per-line free-person counts, and those counts sum to 193 as well. Two independent columns of the same book therefore say 193 and the footing says 198. The reading is not corrected to 198 and the footing is not corrected to 193; both are recorded as written.
column_closure.why_this_matters_for_the_other_seven: The four footed industry columns closing exactly — 4, 15, 18 and 8, on twenty-one entries spread over the whole leaf — is what makes the row grid and the column naming arguable at all. A row grid off by one line, or a column named one place left, would not have closed four columns at once.

the_sequence_screen.what: T-0543's third strand, run to its full extent for the first time. A left sheet's per-line free-person counts and its continuation's TOTAL column are the same numbers in the same order, so they can be compared position for position.
the_sequence_screen.the_two_that_were_arguable: T-0912 named lines 7 and 11 as the two the strip had left arguable. Both are settled here and both agree: line 7 reads 10 and line 11 reads 13. Line 7's figure is a 1 followed by this hand's narrow closed 0 and line 11's is a 1 followed by a 3, both read at 2.2x against the hand's own calibration elsewhere on the leaf.
the_sequence_screen.what_this_is_not: It is not a pairing. T-0543's rule is that the sequence screen corroborates or refuses and never pairs on its own, and that rule is not relaxed here because the agreement came out total.

how_an_entry_was_put_on_a_line: An industry entry is attributed to the line whose TOTAL figure it stands beside, and on this leaf that attribution never needed a judgement: the row grid is uniform at 68.67 px, and every one of the twenty-one industry entries has its ink centre within 26 px of a predicted row centre — a little over a third of the pitch — with the next row centre at least 42 px away. No entry on this leaf is between two lines.

marks_that_are_not_entries.where: line 1, commerce column, near the column's right rule
marks_that_are_not_entries.what: a short bold diagonal stroke about 34 px long
marks_that_are_not_entries.refused_because: it is half the length of this hand's 1, which runs 60 to 90 px on this leaf, and it carries no lead-in. The commerce column's own footing of 4 closes exactly on lines 16, 17 and 25 without it. Recorded as examined and refused, not as a nought and not as an entry.

marks_that_are_not_entries.where: line 18, navigation of the ocean column
marks_that_are_not_entries.what: a short bold stroke, again about a third of a written 1
marks_that_are_not_entries.refused_because: same form and same length as the mark above, and the navigation-of-the-ocean column is footed with an empty cell — the enumerator foots nothing there, which he would not do over a written entry. The manufactures figure on the same line is a separate stroke on the other side of the printed rule and is recorded.

marks_that_are_not_entries.where: the pensioners, deaf/dumb/blind/insane and schools blocks, throughout
marks_that_are_not_entries.what: faint diagonal strokes forming reversed cursive, densest across the seven schools columns
marks_that_are_not_entries.refused_because: SET-OFF — the mirror image of the facing leaf's writing, pressed through while the book was closed. It reads backwards, it runs at a constant lean unrelated to the row grid, it crosses the printed rules without regard to them, and it carries none of the stroke weight of this sheet's ink. Read at 2.4x across the whole right half of the leaf, and at 5x over the schools block: no stroke of the enumerator's weight stands anywhere in those nineteen columns.

blocks_carrying_no_entry.slaves: Twelve columns, thirty-one lines, and not one figure. Read as a block at 1.0x and 2.2x over the whole body: printed rules, paper grain and speckle, and no stroke. Recorded as 0 on every line of every one of the twelve columns, which is what a blank cell means on this form.
blocks_carrying_no_entry.pensioners: NAMES and AGES both empty on every line; no name is written anywhere in the block, and the block is footed blank. Read at 1.1x over both halves of the body.
blocks_carrying_no_entry.deaf_dumb_blind_insane_white: empty on every line of all six columns.
blocks_carrying_no_entry.deaf_dumb_blind_insane_coloured: empty on every line of all four columns.
blocks_carrying_no_entry.schools: empty on every one of the seven columns, and footed blank on all seven. This block carries the heaviest set-off on the leaf and the judgement was made against stroke weight rather than against presence of marks: see marks_that_are_not_entries.

last_column_not_read: The final column of the SCHOOLS bracket — the number of white persons over twenty who cannot read and write — is not in `cells`. Past x3555 the leaf curls into the binding and the exposure falls into the black shadow that carries the next leaf's writing; the column's own rules are not on the image. Declared and unread, and NOT recorded as zero. This is the same declaration 33SQ-GYYJ-9CZ makes about the same column.
records_note: One record per ruled line that enumerates a household, in enumeration order, never reordered. `cells` carries every column of this form that the leaf shows, a blank cell as 0, with pensioners_names as null because the block is empty rather than nought. `total_agrees_with_printed_232` is the position-for-position sequence screen, recorded on the line rather than only in the summary.

pairing.not_ruled_here: This pass did not pair anything and did not re-open the pairing. It read the cells of a leaf already paired, and the one thing it changes about the keys — the TOTAL footing, now 198 rather than 195 — is recorded under the_total_footing_settled with its consequence stated and referred to the owner.
pairing.what_this_reading_changes: Before this pass the project held printed 232's 31 households' names (T-0523) and its left-sheet age-band cells (T-0530), and nothing at all of their family totals, industries, pensions, disabilities or schooling. It now holds all of them. Twenty-one industry entries land on named households for the first time: eight learned professions or engineers, eighteen persons in the navigation of canals, lakes and rivers, fifteen in manufactures and trades, and four in commerce — a shape that is Chicago's own, and one that no other leaf this project has read carries in these proportions.
